_meta.title: AI Compute Demand-Side TAM Parameters
_meta.principle: Four evidence classes: observed = source-reported historical measurement (verification separate); derived = arithmetic; calibrated = chosen using an output target; assumption = judgment, extrapolation or reported forecast. Primary and secondary sources are mixed. Inherited claims are unverified except where explicitly marked.
_meta.structure: Capital scenario, funding shares and merchant allocation. Neither direct chip shipments nor end-customer consumption is measured.
known_definitional_conflicts: Inherited neocloud revenue claims have incompatible populations and dates; retained as context only, never reconciled into a demand total.
Inference share of compute: ~55% of AI INFRASTRUCTURE SPENDING in early 2026 vs Deloitte's ~two-thirds of all AI COMPUTING. Different denominators — dollars vs cycles. Not interchangeable.
Hyperscaler capex: $602B (five largest, CreditSights) vs $600-690B (big four plus ancillary infrastructure). Scope differs on both company count and what counts as ancillary.

hyperscaler_capex_2026_usd_bn.source: CreditSights via Global Data Center Hub

hyperscaler_ai_tied_share.note: Roughly $450B of the $602B is AI-tied. The remainder is general cloud and should not be converted into AI capacity.

hyperscaler_capex_upper_with_ancillary_u.note: Big four north of $600B, some trackers $650-690B including ancillary infrastructure. Midpoint used. Scope differs from the CreditSights figure; do not treat as an upward revision of the same number.

memory_share_of_hyperscaler_ai_spend.note: Fourfold jump from 2023, because inference is memory-bandwidth bound in ways training is not. A composition signal for the training-to-inference shift, visible in the bill of materials.

buyer_segments._note: Who funds AI capacity; these are not accelerator purchase or shipment shares.

hyperscaler_share.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
hyperscaler_share.note: ASSUMPTION. Derived residually: hyperscaler AI capex ~$450B against neocloud and other capital deployment. Sensitivity 0.62-0.80.

neocloud_share.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
neocloud_share.note: ASSUMPTION, anchored on observed neocloud contracted power and financing scale rather than on revenue. Neoclouds deploy capital far ahead of revenue, so a revenue-based share would understate their chip buying materially.

enterprise_and_sovereign_share.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
enterprise_and_sovereign_share.note: ASSUMPTION. Enterprise self-build plus sovereign programmes. The weakest-evidenced segment in the model.

revenue_2025_usd_bn.note: Q4 2025 alone reached $9B, up 223% YoY. See definitional conflict note in _meta.

revenue_2030_forecast_usd_bn.note: Approaching $400B by 2031, implying roughly 58% CAGR. A forecast, not an observation of the market.

coreweave_active_power_gw.note: Contracted power roughly 3.7-4.2 GW across 51 data centers. Active power is the revenue-bearing figure.

coreweave_backlog_usd_bn.note: Remaining performance obligations. Roughly eight years of revenue at the current guide, which is why backlog is the promise and debt is the fact.

coreweave_take_or_pay_share.note: Contracts are 2-5 year take-or-pay. Customers pay regardless of usage, which decouples PROVIDER revenue from CONSUMER utilization. Central to the model: booked demand is contractual, not consumptive.

customer_concentration_top3.note: Microsoft was 67% of CoreWeave 2025 revenue. Top three expected to remain above 80% even after diversification.

revenue_per_gw_year_usd_bn.source: Derived from CoreWeave FY2026 revenue guide over active power
revenue_per_gw_year_usd_bn.note: Illustrative $8.5bn per occupied GW-year proxy, loosely based on FY guidance divided by a point-in-time active-power figure. Periods differ. Not a realized yield, contracted revenue forecast, or evidence that energization means consumption.

capex_per_gw_usd_bn.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
capex_per_gw_usd_bn.note: Calibrated in the original module partly to a supply-output comparison. Retained at $35bn/GW without retuning. That comparison was not independent and its delivery benchmark was stock, so no validation claim remains.

coreweave_h100_gpu_hour_usd.note: Roughly 60% above Nebius and Lambda published rates. SemiAnalysis puts the premium at 10-15% on a like-for-like basis, so the headline gap overstates it.

breakeven_utilization.note: Inherited illustrative estimate, not an operator disclosure or explanation of contracting choices. Context only.

consumption._note: Who is CONSUMING COMPUTE. Different population from the chip buyers above.

inference_share_of_infra_spend_2026.note: Up from about 33% in 2023. Denominator is infrastructure SPENDING.

inference_share_of_compute_cycles_2026.note: Denominator is compute CYCLES. Not the same as the spend measure above and must not be substituted for it.

inference_share_of_lifecycle_dollars.note: Inherited midpoint of an 80–90% lifecycle spending estimate. Context only; not a measured GW allocation.

gartner_ai_cloud_market_2026_usd_bn.note: AI-optimized infrastructure spending, roughly 15% of a $287.3B IaaS market. Inference claims $23.3B of it — the first year inference beats training.

agentic_token_multiplier_low.note: Tokens per task versus a standard chatbot interaction.

agentic_token_multiplier_high.note: Each task fans out into reasoning steps, tool calls and retries.

cost_per_interaction_agentic_usd.note: Roughly 30x the linear workflow. Per-token price fell; tokens per transaction exploded.

token_price_decline_2yr_factor.source: Stanford HAI AI Index via Telnyx
token_price_decline_2yr_factor.note: GPT-3.5-equivalent MMLU query cost fell from $20.00 to roughly $0.07 per million tokens over about two years.

enterprise_spend_growth_same_period.note: Inherited 3.2x multiplier retained as context. Original 'rose 320%' wording conflicts (would imply 4.2x); no causal capacity-pricing inference is used.

deployment_mode._note: The bridge between chip buyers and compute consumers. Determines who owns capacity and who captures margin.

hyperscaler_self_consumed_share.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
hyperscaler_self_consumed_share.note: ASSUMPTION. Share of hyperscaler-bought capacity consumed internally rather than resold. The remainder is sold as cloud, which makes hyperscalers both buyers and landlords.

neocloud_resold_share.note: Stylized assumption that all neocloud capacity is resold. Does not establish actual utilization.

hyperscalers_renting_from_neoclouds.source: Microsoft $60B+ in neocloud commitments; Meta up to $62B across CoreWeave and Nebius
hyperscalers_renting_from_neoclouds.note: The flow is not one-directional. Hyperscalers buy chips AND rent capacity, because they cannot build fast enough. This is the demand-side reflection of the supply module's delivery constraint.

enterprise_merchant_share.note: Assume enterprise/sovereign self-build is outside merchant demand; expose the formerly implicit exclusion.

us_capacity_share.note: Illustrative US share of company-wide capex-implied capacity; geographic bridge, not a measured share.

merchant_supply_share.note: Independent supply ownership assumption, not mechanically copied from demand shares.

demand_growth.note: Annual US merchant capacity requirement multiplier.

live_load_weights.note: Weights for energized capacity becoming ready for occupancy, lag 0 and 1. Readiness is not actual IT electricity consumption; matched demand determines modeled occupation.

capacity_required_weights.note: Capex cohort to requested-service year allocation, lag 0 and 1; independent of energized ramp.

opening_merchant_capex_gw.note: Illustrative US merchant capex-implied cohort before forecast start; supplies the opening requested-service tail.

horizon_years.note: Default reporting horizon; origin stored separately.

h1_annualization_factor.note: Assume H2 equals H1 to initialize signing flow, not delivery-year demand.

opening_demand_backlog_gw.note: Unmet service requested before origin excluded; explicit initial balance.

opening_ready_capacity_gw.note: No spare capacity from pre-origin energizations. This is an incremental model.

existing_occupied_capacity_gw.note: Existing fleet excluded; all occupied totals track incremental cohorts only.

cancellation_rate.note: No cancellation implemented; nonzero value rejected rather than silently ignored.

retirement_rate.note: No retirement implemented; nonzero value rejected rather than silently ignored.

capex_sensitivity.note: Cost per GW scenarios; preserve contrary outcomes.

geography_sensitivity.note: US share scenarios, not a confidence interval.

customer_segment_mix._note: Funding ownership shares, not end-consumer or chip-shipment shares. All paths are assumptions. Annual interpolation is derived arithmetic; no path is calibrated to supply or to a preferred conclusion.

end_year.source: Explicit scenario design; no external observation
end_year.note: Last supported year. Do not silently extrapolate.

terminal_shares.source: Explicit scenario design; no external observation
terminal_shares.note: Order: hyperscaler, neocloud, enterprise/sovereign. Linear paths from registered 2026 shares. Base represents modest diversification; alternatives stress ownership concentration, resale growth, and self-build growth. Magnitudes are illustrative judgments, not estimates, probabilities or fitted outputs. static-control holds opening shares throughout.
